hints: Look at each statement separately and ask what oxidation number changes, if any, are happening.
Remember that $\text{Cl}^-$ from NaCl gives only $\text{HCl}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, with no change in oxidation state from -1.
Check how $\text{Cl}_2$ behaves with cold alkali and with water, and track where oxidation number 0 goes to decide on disproportionation and acidity.
walkthrough:
**Test statement 1 - NaCl + concentrated acid**

Think acid-base first, redox second. Chloride is a weak reducing agent and is not oxidised by concentrated sulfuric acid.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{NaCl(s) + H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(l) } \rightarrow \text{ NaHSO}_4\text{(s) + HCl(g)}$$

**Test statement 2 - Chlorine + cold NaOH**

Disproportionation means the same element is both oxidised and reduced. Here $\text{Cl}_2$ starts at 0 and splits two ways.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{NaCl + NaClO + H}_2\text{O}$$

**Test statement 3 - Chlorine + water**

Chlorine reacts reversibly with water to give two acids, so the solution is acidic.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{Cl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{HCl + HClO}$$

**Combine the verdicts**

Statement 1 is false, statements 2 and 3 are true. So the correct combination is 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 is wrong because $\text{Cl}^-$ stays at oxidation state -1 in $\text{HCl}$, it is not oxidised to $\text{Cl}_2$. Only $\text{Br}^-$ and $\text{I}^-$ are strong enough reducing agents to be oxidised by concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.
options.B: Incorrect. This option claims 1 and 2 only are correct. Statement 2 is correct but statement 1 is not, and it wrongly leaves out statement 3 which is correct.
options.C: Correct. Statement 2 is true because $\text{Cl}$ (0) goes to -1 in $\text{NaCl}$ and +1 in $\text{NaClO}$, a clear disproportionation. Statement 3 is true because $\text{HCl}$, a strong acid, plus $\text{HClO}$ make the solution acidic. Statement 1 is false.
options.D: Incorrect. This option does not select 2 and 3 together. Any option including statement 1 is wrong, and any option omitting statement 2 or statement 3 misses a true reaction.
